fatal_errors: The proposed Nb–Ti–Al–Zr composition, FCC/B2 lamellar structure, and thermomechanical treatment do not reconstruct the Cr-modified HfMoTaTiZr system or its reticulated Laves-phase mechanism.
Neither cited study supports the specified 850 °C rolling, 50% reduction, 30–50 s annealing, 1000 °C performance, or predicted 20–25% strength increase.

E1 concerns an Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni eutectic alloy tested primarily at room temperature, while E2 concerns single-BCC Ti–Al–Cr–Nb–V–Zr medium-entropy alloys; neither establishes coherent FCC/B2 lamellae in Nb–Ti–Al–Zr.
The claimed FCC constituent in the proposed refractory Nb–Ti–Al–Zr alloy is asserted without phase-equilibrium or experimental support.
The baseline is underspecified because 'as-cast or coarser-structured counterparts' can represent materially different comparison states.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses the application-level request by proposing a density-neutral processing intervention, high-temperature testing, and preservation of room-temperature ductility. Its experiment is reasonably falsifiable because it directly measures microstructure, high-temperature yield strength, and room-temperature ductility against a baseline. However, it has essentially no agreement with the hidden target: it changes the alloy system and intervention, predicts an FCC/B2 lamellar mediator rather than a reticulated Cr-rich Laves phase, uses different loading and temperature conditions, and omits the target's simultaneous room-temperature increases in yield strength and fracture strain. More importantly, the quantitative processing recipe and performance prediction are not supported by the cited evidence. The references offer only distant analogies and do not validate the proposed phase constitution or high-temperature response, so the alternative remains insufficiently evidenced rather than a well-supported plausible alternative.
